quotes.text: Your past has a way of sneaking up on you. You'll hear broken echoes of it everywhere, like a bad replay. You'll get mad at everyone for reminding you about it, even if it's all in your head.
The sun went down with practiced bravado. Twilight crawled across the sky, laden with foreboding.
I lied to myself that it was over. I was still alive, my loved ones were still dead. It wasn't over.
It was a classic mob hit. No worries. No fuss. Just another page in the obituaries.
When had I ever needed to invite trouble in? It always found me, no matter where I hid.
Max, we got to stop meeting like this.
One thing left to do. I was compelled to give Vlad his gun back. One bullet at a time.
So much for a lazy Sunday afternoon.
There it was — the soundtrack to my life. And, for a few seconds, came harmony. Finally...
He had a baseball bat, and I was tied to a chair. Pissing him off was the smart thing to do.
I had a hole in my second favorite drinking arm, and the only way out of the frozen storage was through the loading bay.
The past is a gaping hole. You try to run from it, but the more you run, the deeper, more terrible it grows behind you, its edges yawning at your heels.
One thing you can count on: You push a man too far, and sooner or later he'll start pushing back.
I don't know about angels, but it's fear that gives men wings.
Another dark, rainy night. Another police station. Another futile crusade for amends. Time moves forward, and nothing changes.

All this time we got the fable of Sleeping Beauty wrong. The prince didn't kiss her to wake her up. No one who slept for a hundred years is likely to wake up. It was the other way round. He kisses her to wake himself up from the nightmare that has brought him there.
I had a bullet. I had a gun. Time to go to work.
He was trying to buy more sand for his hourglass. I wasn't selling any.

Einstein was right, time is relative to the observer. When you're looking down the barrel of a gun, time slows down. Your whole life flashes by, heartbreak and scars. Stay with it, and you can live a lifetime in that split second.
Nothing is a cliché when it's happening to you.

Life was good. The sun setting on a sweet summer's day, the smell of freshly mowed lawns, the sounds of children playing — A house across the river, on the Jersey-side. A beautiful wife and a baby girl. The American Dream come true. But dreams have a nasty habit of going bad when you're not looking.
I was still alive, and still not all that happy about it.
There are no choices. Nothing but a straight line. The illusion comes afterwards, when you ask 'Why me?' and 'What if?'
Collecting evidence had gotten old a few hundred bullets back. I was already so far beyond the point of no return I couldn't even remember what it had looked like when I had passed it.
God, I turned out to be such a damsel in distress.
I was in a New York minute. In a New York minute, everything can change.
The way I see it there's two types of people: those who spend their lives trying to build a future and those who spend their lives trying to rebuild the past.
I hadn't slept in a million years.
I had a dream of my wife. She was dead. But it was all right.
Like all the bad things in my life, it started with the death of a woman. I couldn't save her.
